architecture_decisions.recommendation: Changed the default value of `heartbeat_frequency` from `None` to `180` seconds in the FlowsSettings model to enable heartbeat detection by default
architecture_decisions.rationale: This change makes the system more resilient out-of-the-box by enabling automatic detection of zombie/crashed flow runs without requiring user configuration. The 180-second (3-minute) interval provides a reasonable balance between detection latency and system overhead.
alternatives_considered: Keeping heartbeats disabled by default (previous behavior)
Using a different default interval (e.g., 60 seconds for faster detection but more overhead)
Making heartbeats mandatory without ability to disable

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Maintained `Optional[int]` type for `heartbeat_frequency` and allowed `None` value to disable heartbeats
architecture_decisions.rationale: Users who explicitly want to disable heartbeats can still do so by setting `PREFECT_FLOWS_HEARTBEAT_FREQUENCY` to `null` or `None`. This preserves existing workflows while improving defaults for new users.
alternatives_considered: Adding a separate boolean flag to enable/disable heartbeats
Deprecating the ability to disable heartbeats

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated the JSON schema to reflect the new default value and maintained the same validation constraints
architecture_decisions.rationale: The JSON schema is auto-generated from the Pydantic models, so updating the model automatically updates the schema. This ensures documentation, API clients, and configuration UIs show the correct default value.
alternatives_considered: Manually updating the schema without model changes
Not updating the schema (would cause inconsistencies)

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added event retention overrides for heartbeat events with a 7-day retention period
architecture_decisions.rationale: Heartbeat events will now be generated by default, so they need appropriate retention policies. The 7-day retention for `prefect.flow-run.heartbeat` events allows for debugging and monitoring while preventing unlimited growth.
alternatives_considered: Using the global event retention period for all events

tickets.title: Enable flow heartbeat detection by default
tickets.description: Update the default configuration to enable flow run heartbeat monitoring with a 180-second interval, allowing automatic detection of crashed flow runs without user configuration

implementation_summary:
The implementation enables flow heartbeat detection by default across the Prefect orchestration platform. The core change modifies the `FlowsSettings` model in `src/prefect/settings/models/flows.py` to set `heartbeat_frequency` from `None` (disabled) to `180` seconds. This change automatically propagates to the JSON schema in `schemas/settings.schema.json`, ensuring consistent documentation and client behavior.

Key design decisions include maintaining backward compatibility by keeping the field as `Optional[int]`, allowing users to disable heartbeats by setting the value to `None`. The 180-second interval was chosen as a reasonable default that balances detection speed with system overhead. Additionally, the implementation includes related infrastructure changes: the database vacuum service configuration was updated to support event-specific retention policies, with heartbeat events (`prefect.flow-run.heartbeat`) configured for 7-day retention by default.

The changes integrate seamlessly with the existing settings management system built on Pydantic models. The auto-generated JSON schema ensures that all configuration interfaces (CLI, UI, API) reflect the new defaults. This approach follows the established pattern in Prefect's configuration system where sensible defaults are provided but can be overridden through environment variables or explicit configuration.
